text:
Dear Mr Dyer,

Thank you for returning the lunch registration form for Jasper. From Monday 16 November he joins the hot lunch rota at Ysgol Bryn Celyn.

You told us he has a severe allergy to sesame and a milder reaction to raw celery. His adrenaline pen stays in the school office, and the kitchen must not serve him anything from the bakery tray, even if it looks plain. He may have the pasta bake only if the kitchen confirms the sauce contains neither.

Jasper's dinner account still shows 38.40 pounds owing for last half term. You can pay online or send cash in a named envelope, but we cannot top up the account until the arrears are cleared, and hot lunches stop after 31 December if the balance is unpaid. You mentioned you may ask about help with costs if your hours at the garage are cut in the new year.

If anything changes, please ring Eirlys Beynon in the kitchen on 01632 960417.

Kind regards,
Rhiannon Pugh
School office

text:
Coach Osian Thackeray stopped me after Tuesday training. Gwenllian has been sitting out sprint drills since half term because her left knee swells up after hard matches, and her physio, Imogen Fairbrother, wants her limited to 30 minutes per game until the scan result comes back. Osian said he will rotate her on and off and will not pick her for the full 70-minute cup tie unless the physio clears her in writing.

The under-12s spring fee is 85 pounds, due by 5 December. I paid 40 by bank transfer on the 14th, so 45 is left. Winifred Bate, the club treasurer, said families who are short can apply to the hardship fund, and I may ask about it if my shifts at the depot stay as short as this month.

The next away match is Saturday 21 November at Llanfair Rovers, kick-off 10:30, with the minibus leaving the clubhouse at 8:45. Players need shin pads, a water bottle and the signed consent form, and the manager will text by 7:30 if the pitch is frozen.

text:
Met Lucinda Marsh, the family liaison officer at Ysgol Pen-y-Bryn, about Dylan's lunches. He has been refusing school dinners since September, and the cook says he leaves most of the food. We agreed he will try a packed lunch on Mondays and Wednesdays and school dinners on the other days, and she will tell me if he skips them again.

Dylan lives with me from Sunday to Thursday and with his father, Edmund Thorne, on Fridays and every second weekend, so the Friday lunch order comes from Edmund's side. Lucinda suggested a shared note in his bag listing what he ate, and I said Edmund would only agree to that if it goes through the school office, not through me.

The school also confirmed that Dylan qualifies for free school meals from January because my universal credit claim went through, so the 2.60 pounds daily charge stops on 5 January. Until then I should keep paying through the school app on Sunday evenings.

text: The nightly sync between the orders database and the invoicing service failed on 3 and 4 November because the queue worker ran out of memory after the batch size was raised from 500 to 2,000 rows. Rolling the batch size back to 500 on the 5th fixed it, and Nathan Pickersgill confirmed the retry job now finishes in about 40 minutes. We owe the customer, Penrose Veterinary Group, service credits of 3,150 euros under the 99.5 percent uptime clause because the failure lasted 31 hours. Seren Cadwallader approved paying for an extra worker node at 190 euros a month until the code fix ships, but only if the credits are not disputed. The fix, which streams rows instead of loading them all, is scheduled for release 4.18 on 20 November.
